title: Platform operations: online update, single sign-on and private networking
html:
Who this page is for: the organiser or platform administrator who keeps this console running after the event. Participants do not need it. The three sections are independent; read the one you need: section 1 upgrades the console to a new version, section 2 lets employees sign in with IAM Identity Center, section 3 explains what network profiles and storage locations need prepared on the AWS side and how to troubleshoot them.

Prerequisites

  • The console's admin account. Section 1 happens in the console only.
  • Section 2 also needs an IAM Identity Center instance with permission to add applications, and Session Manager access to the console instance (Organizer deployment guide, section 11).
  • Section 3 needs permission to create endpoints, access points or file systems in this account's VPC.

1. Update the console online

The console instance has an updater installed (by the stack's user-data). An administrator prepares a new version beside the running service from the console, then picks a time to restart onto it — no login to the instance. A failed upgrade returns to the old version automatically.

  1. As admin, open Modules → Configuration → System update (/v3/system-update). The page header says "New commits of console-v3 from https://github.com/aws-samples/sample-agentcore-launchpad…". Click Check now. Expected result: the Running version and Latest console-v3 cards show commit ids; when behind, the page shows "N commit(s) behind" and the Commits list, otherwise Up to date; Updater reads Installed.

    In the image: 1 Running version eda8adf; 2 Latest console-v3, up to date; 3 History, one row per update. When there are new commits, a Commits list also appears below 2.

  2. Click Prepare update. The updater runs Fetch, Check out, Backend dependencies, Frontend build, Import check, Start check and Disk check; when all pass the status is Ready. The running console is not affected.

  3. Under Restart time, choose Now (in one minute) or At a time. If tasks are in progress (evaluation runs, deploys, release gates), the page lists "N task(s) in progress, M interrupted by the restart" and what happens to each one after the restart (resumes, reconciles, fails, …); tick "I know … will be interrupted" before you can schedule. Click Schedule restart. Expected result: "Restart scheduled; an announcement tells users", and every user sees an announcement at the top of the page until the update ends.

  4. After the restart, reload the page: the commit id at the bottom left is the new version and the entry in History reads Succeeded. In this run the update from 03df354 to e246cf7 (17 commits) took about 1 minute to prepare and about 2 minutes to restart after scheduling Now. On 2026-10-23, in the us-west-2 environment, the update from ce2dbfc to eda8adf (4 commits) took about 2 min 20 s from Prepare update to the new commit id at the bottom left; History keeps one row per update, and the image shows this environment's three.

To go back, click Roll back: it prepares the version the last update replaced and applies it through Schedule restart as well. Only fast-forward updates are accepted; otherwise the page shows "Not a fast-forward — refused".

Make sure no long task is running before you schedule. Tasks that step 3 lists as "fails" or "stranded" must be started again after the restart.

2. Single sign-on with IAM Identity Center (SAML 2.0)

IAM Identity Center offers a customer managed SAML 2.0 application. Once connected, employees click Continue with <name> on the console's login page or open the app tile in the AWS access portal. Accounts are created at first sign-in; global and project roles follow Identity Center groups.

2.1 Tell the backend the console's public address first

The SP entity ID and ACS URL are built from the backend setting public_base_url (environment variable LAUNCHPAD_PUBLIC_BASE_URL), whose default http://localhost:5173 Identity Center cannot post to. The instance does not know the CloudFront domain when it boots (the distribution uses the instance as its origin and is created after it), so the current template runs Run Command once the distribution exists (stack resource PublicBaseUrlAssociation): it writes LAUNCHPAD_PUBLIC_BASE_URL=<ConsoleUrl> to /etc/launchpad-public.env and restarts the backend. Check it on the Single sign-on page first: after you create a provider, its ACS URL should start with <ConsoleUrl>.

On a stack deployed from an earlier template, or with a ParticipantRoleArn that has no SSM permissions (Run Command then stays pending), the ACS URL still starts with http://localhost:5173; set it by hand as below (that is how this run's stack was fixed: the API's ACS template went from http://localhost:5173/api/auth/saml/{id}/acs to <ConsoleUrl>/api/auth/saml/{id}/acs):

  1. Open a Session Manager terminal as in section 11 of the Organizer deployment guide.

  2. Replace <ConsoleUrl> with the stack output ConsoleUrl (like https://dxxxxxxxx.cloudfront.net, no trailing /) and paste the whole block at once:

    bash
    echo 'LAUNCHPAD_PUBLIC_BASE_URL=<ConsoleUrl>' | sudo tee -a /etc/launchpad-auth.env >/dev/null && \
sudo systemctl restart launchpad-backend && \
curl -s --retry 10 --retry-connrefused --retry-delay 1 localhost:8000/api/health

Expected result: {"status":"ok",…}. Back on the Single sign-on page, the addresses of a new provider start with <ConsoleUrl>.

2.2 Create the provider in the console

  1. As admin, open Modules → Configuration → Single sign-on (/v3/sso), click New provider and choose AWS IAM Identity Center. The name is the text on the login button, for example Company SSO. Click Create. Expected result: "<name> created — fill in the connection, test it, then enable it". The provider starts disabled; local accounts keep signing in.
  2. On the provider's page, The console gives the IdP lists three values. Keep the page open:
    • SP entity ID: <ConsoleUrl>/api/auth/saml/<id>/metadata
    • ACS URL: <ConsoleUrl>/api/auth/saml/<id>/acs
    • SP metadata: an XML file with the same values

2.3 Add the application in Identity Center

  1. In the IAM Identity Center console: Applications → Add application → I have an application I want to set up → SAML 2.0.

  2. Display name: Launchpad console. Under IAM Identity Center metadata, copy the IAM Identity Center SAML metadata file URL.

  3. Application properties (optional): Application start URL <ConsoleUrl>/api/auth/saml/<id>/start makes the portal tile start a normal SP-initiated sign-in. Leave Relay state empty.

  4. Application metadata: upload the console's SP metadata file, or choose Manually type your metadata values with Application ACS URL = the ACS URL and Application SAML audience = the SP entity ID.

  5. Submit, then open the application's Actions → Edit attribute mappings:

    User attribute in the application Maps to this string value Format
    Subject ${user:subject} persistent
    email ${user:email} unspecified
    name ${user:name} unspecified
    groups ${user:groups} unspecified

    Subject becomes the account's key in the console; use the stable Identity Center user id, not the email, which can change. email is required; the console username is the part of the email before @.

  6. Assign users and groups: only people assigned to the application can sign in.

2.4 Load the metadata, map groups, enable

  1. Back on the provider's page in the console, under The IdP gives the console, paste the metadata URL and click Load. The console reads the IdP entity ID, the SSO URL and the signing certificate, and shows how long the certificate stays valid. Click Test connection.
  2. Keep the defaults: Allow IdP-initiated sign-in on (the portal tile works); Sign requests off; Require encrypted assertions off (Identity Center does not encrypt assertions for customer managed applications, so with it on every sign-in is refused).
  3. Group mappings: ${user:groups} sends group ids (GUIDs), not names. Enter the value from Groups → <group> → Group ID in Identity Center and choose the global role or project role it grants (project groups are retired; an old project-group mapping is rewritten into mappings to its projects on upgrade) — for example map an "after-sales business" group to the biz_owner project role template in project retail-service. Mappings apply at every sign-in; a role an administrator set by hand wins.
  4. In Accounts, keep jit (create accounts at first sign-in); you can add an email-domain allowlist.
  5. Click Enable. Expected result: "<name> is on the login page"; the login page shows Continue with <name> and the app tile appears in each assigned user's AWS access portal.

Identity Center does not push users (SCIM) to customer managed SAML applications, so group changes take effect at the user's next sign-in. To cut someone's access at once, disable the account in User Management. With the Sign-in page set to Single sign-on only, the built-in administrator can still sign in with the local password at <ConsoleUrl>/?local=1.

2.5 When a sign-in fails

A refused sign-in returns to the login page with a reason; the provider's Recent sign-ins and the audit action auth.sso.login record the same code:

Reason Usual cause
auth.saml.bad_audience Application SAML audience is not exactly the SP entity ID
auth.saml.bad_destination Application ACS URL differs, or LAUNCHPAD_PUBLIC_BASE_URL changed after setup
auth.saml.bad_signature / unsigned Identity Center rotated its certificate — Load the metadata again
auth.saml.expired The instance clock is more than 2 minutes off
auth.saml.unsolicited The portal tile was used while IdP-initiated sign-in is off
auth.saml.in_response_to The login page was left open over 10 minutes, or the response was replayed
auth.sso.email_missing The email attribute mapping is missing
auth.sso.not_provisioned The account policy is existing_only and this user has no linked account yet

3. Network profiles and storage locations: what to prepare on the AWS side

The Platform configuration chapter has participants read Network profiles (/v3/network) and Storage (/v3/storage). Both kinds of record only reference existing AWS resources: the platform does not create VPCs, subnets, endpoints, NAT gateways, access points or file systems. To actually run an agent in a VPC or mount a file system, the organiser prepares them on the AWS side first.

3.1 Agents in a VPC

  • Interface endpoints: when the agent subnets have no NAT, they must at least reach logs (without it logs and traces are silently lost; the profile check lists it as blocking); a missing xray is a warning. Every other service the agent uses (bedrock-runtime, bedrock-agentcore, the s3 gateway endpoint, secretsmanager, …) also needs an endpoint or NAT. The workshop stack already created the endpoints the console needs in its own VPC; a different VPC for agents needs its own.
  • Check: on the profile's detail page click Check and read each blocking, warning and informational item. The informational item inbound.endpoint reports whether the VPC has the AgentCore data-plane endpoint (com.amazonaws.<region>.bedrock-agentcore) that internal systems use to call agents privately; the informational item cost counts interface endpoints × availability zones and the NAT gateways on the route. Price them with the regional price list; the platform does not estimate.
  • Teardown order: delete every agent that uses the profile first. For each deleted VPC agent the platform waits for AgentCore to release its ENIs in the subnets (up to 6 hours); meanwhile the profile cannot be archived (network_profile.enis_pending). Once all ENIs are gone, archive the profile, then delete the subnets, security groups and endpoints. Archiving while an agent still uses the profile returns network_profile.in_use.

3.2 Storage locations

  • A storage location registers an existing S3 Files or EFS access point with a maximum mode (ro / rw). Only administrators register, check and delete locations; members pick a location in the deploy wizard and cannot mount it above its maximum mode.
  • Mounting needs the agent in a VPC that reaches the file system, so prepare the network profile from 3.1 first. On mount the platform adds the inline policy launchpad-fs-<agent> to the agent's execution role and removes it when the agent is deleted.
  • The platform never deletes a file system or access point. After the event, the organiser deletes the ones they created in the S3 / EFS console.

Checklist

  • System update shows Updater Installed, and a check shows the running version and the latest commit
  • (if you did section 2) the backend's public_base_url is ConsoleUrl, and Identity Center users sign in from the login page and the access portal
  • (if you did section 3) the profile check has no blocking item, and the profile archives after its VPC agents are deleted

FAQ

Symptom Cause Fix
System update shows Apply by hand and a list of commands The updater is not installed on the instance Run sudo backend/scripts/install_updater.sh on the instance, or update by hand with the commands shown
System update says "Online update is turned off on this host" Environment variable LAUNCHPAD_UPDATE_ENABLED=false Upgrade by hand as in section 11 of the Organizer deployment guide
Status Prepare failed A self-check step failed (for example low disk or a failed build) Open Log to see the failing step; the running version is not affected
The SSO provider's ACS URL starts with http://localhost:5173 The stack comes from an earlier template, or Run Command did not run Set it by hand as in 2.1 and restart the backend
Everyone fails to sign in after turning on Require encrypted assertions Identity Center does not encrypt assertions for customer managed applications Turn the option off
